# TDPdf v1.28.1.0

**Editing text in place on a form could permanently erase the border lines next to it — that's fixed, and the tool now has the same font, color, move and resize controls as a placed text box.**

## What was broken

Editing existing text on a PDF — double-clicking a value already printed on the page and typing a replacement, as opposed to placing a brand-new text annotation — painted an opaque white rectangle over the original text to hide it. On a tightly spaced form, like a table row tracking a claimed count, that rectangle could bleed into the row's border lines and erase them with no way to undo it: the box had no font or color picker, and dragging it to move or resize did nothing at all, even though it looked selectable. The Select tool's click handling was in fact filtering these edits out of consideration entirely, so a plain click could never select one in the first place.

## What changed

- Editing existing text now gets the same style bar as a placed text box: font size and color are adjustable after the fact.
- The box can be moved and resized like any other annotation — useful for pulling a too-generous whiteout back in by hand, or nudging text that landed slightly off.
- The default whiteout is drawn with half the previous overhang, so it hugs the detected text more closely before you ever touch it.

Nothing about *placing new* text annotations changes — Insert Text already had all of this.
